text_en: French Finance Minister Lescure said on Friday that France's economy will grow less than expected this year, and the government will also be unable to meet its budget deficit target. Lescure said he lowered the government's economic growth forecast for 2026 to 0.5% from 0.7% previously, but maintained next year's growth forecast of 1.0%. "This year has experienced an extremely severe crisis involving four different types of shocks," Lescure said, citing factors such as domestic political uncertainty, soaring energy prices, extreme summer weather, and surging bond market borrowing costs. The downgrade to the economic outlook makes the government's task in the coming months of pushing the 2027 budget through a severely divided parliament even more difficult. Parties have already taken tough positions ahead of the two rounds of presidential elections to be held from April to May.
